title: End-to-End Testing Concepts
learning_outcomes: Describe the purpose and main behavior of end-to-end testing concepts.
Apply end-to-end testing concepts in a small Python example or interpret a representative result.
Identify one limitation, edge case, compatibility concern, or failure mode relevant to the topic.

content.intro: This lesson introduces end-to-end testing concepts as part of testing, debugging, and code quality. It turns the curriculum heading into a short, practical concept guide with a visual, example, and checks to try locally.
content.why_it_matters: Reliable software expects mistakes and failures. Reproduce the smallest failing case, assert the intended behavior, and fix the cause rather than hiding the symptom.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Reliable software expects mistakes and failures. Reproduce the smallest failing case, assert the intended behavior, and fix the cause rather than hiding the symptom.

content_blocks.title: How to work with it
content_blocks.text: For end-to-end testing concepts, identify the inputs and assumptions first. Use the smallest useful example, predict its behavior, run it in a local Python interpreter, and compare the observed result with your prediction. The example below is a static reference in CodeLeaf, not executed Python.

content_blocks.code:
def double(value):
    return value * 2

assert double(4) == 8
print("Checks passed")
content_blocks.run_instructions: Run with python main.py. For a maintained project, move assertions into a test module and use the project test runner.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original snippet, run it in your local interpreter, and compare the result with the documented reference output. Do not assume the CodeLeaf editor executed it.

content_blocks.title: Version and reliability note
content_blocks.text: Use the interpreter and dependencies declared for your project. Where a feature is version-specific or tool-dependent, check its official documentation and document a useful fallback.

content.task: Try it yourself: adapt the example to demonstrate end-to-end testing concepts with different inputs. Write down your prediction, run it locally, and explain the result plus one edge case.
task_acceptance_criteria: Explain the central idea in end-to-end testing concepts without copying the definition.
Run or manually verify the smallest example using the stated runtime assumptions.
Describe one relevant edge case, limitation, or troubleshooting step.
hints: Read the sample carefully and identify the values or state that affect the result.
Change one variable or input at a time and predict what should happen before running it.
Check the official reference and runtime version if behavior differs from the expected result.
